name: mimic

special_abilities.name: shapechanger
special_abilities.desc: The mimic can use its action to polymorph into an object or back into its true, amorphous form. Its statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn 't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

special_abilities.name: adhesive (object form only)
special_abilities.desc: The mimic adheres to anything that touches it. A Huge or smaller creature adhered to the mimic is also grappled by it (escape DC 13). Ability checks made to escape this grapple have disadvantage.

special_abilities.name: false appearance (object form only)
special_abilities.desc: While the mimic remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from an ordinary object.

special_abilities.name: grappler
special_abilities.desc: The mimic has advantage on attack rolls against any creature grappled by it.

actions.name: pseudopod
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage. If the mimic is in object form, the target is subjected to its Adhesive trait.

actions.name: bite
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage plus 4 (1d8) acid damage.

lore:
The Mimic, or *Pseudopodus vorax*, is a master of the mundane. It resides in the forgotten corners of the world—damp crypts, dusty manors, and the shadowed ruins of fallen empires. Unlike the feral beasts of the wild, the Mimic thrives on the proximity of civilization, adopting the forms of chests, doors, or even humble barrels to blend seamlessly into its environment.

Its predatory method is a testament to lethal patience. The creature secretes a powerful, resinous adhesive, binding the unwary traveler to its deceptive hide the moment contact is made. Once its prey is ensnared, the Mimic unfolds into a nightmare of undulating flesh and jagged, crystalline teeth. It does not hunt; it waits for the victim’s own curiosity or greed to seal their fate.

In local folklore, the Mimic is often dubbed "The Mirror of Avarice." Village elders tell tales of the "Gilded Trap" to warn children against taking what is not theirs. It is whispered that a Mimic is a manifestation of the world’s malice toward those who seek easy riches. To the seasoned scholar, it remains a grim reminder: in the dark, even the most familiar object can possess a hunger.
